sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Pennsylvania, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

Your application must be RECEIVED by your county election office by 5 p.m. on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 (the rule: at least one week before the election). After that, a voter with an emergency (an unexpected illness or disability, or a last-minute absence from their municipality) can apply for an emergency absentee ballot until 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your county election office must RECEIVE your completed ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A postmark by that time is not enough. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Tuesday, October 27, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Pennsylvania’s own site

At school away from home, in Pennsylvania or in another state? What Pennsylvania says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered voter may ask for a no-excuse mail-in ballot. Pennsylvania also has the absentee ballot, for voters who will be out of their municipality on Election Day or have an illness or disability that keeps them from the polls; it asks for the reason. Both work the same way after that. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply online with a valid Pennsylvania driver's license, PennDOT photo ID, or the last 4 digits of your Social Security number. Give an email address to get updates on your ballot. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Download the paper mail-in (or absentee) application, fill it in and mail it to your county election office. You can also ask your county, email the Department of State, or call 1-877-VOTESPA for a paper application. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Once your county's ballots are ready, apply at your county election office (or another official site) and get your ballot right away; you can even fill it in and hand it back in the same visit. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it back in the pre-addressed outer envelope, early enough to arrive by 8 p.m. on November 3. (official page)
  • Drop box. Some counties have drop boxes; the state lists each county's return locations. (official page)
  • In person. Your county election office during its business hours, or another official location, before 8 p.m. on Election Day. You must return your own ballot; only a voter with a disability who has named someone in writing on the state's form may have another person deliver it. (official page)

What the envelope needs

To apply you give your Pennsylvania driver's license or PennDOT ID number; if you have neither, the last four digits of your Social Security number; if you have none of these, a copy of a photo ID such as a U.S. passport, a U.S. military ID, a government employee photo ID, or a photo employee ID from a Pennsylvania college or university. On the ballot: seal it in the yellow envelope marked "official election ballot" with no marks on it, seal that inside the outer return envelope, then SIGN AND WRITE THE DATE on the voter's declaration on the outside. The state says a ballot without the completed declaration will not be counted. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Pennsylvania’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Pennsylvania has no early voting at polling places. Instead, once your county's ballots are ready you can apply for a mail ballot at your county election office, fill it in and hand it back in one visit; applications are due by 5 p.m. on October 27, 2026. Election Day polls are open on November 3. (official page)

Students

At school in Pennsylvania, away from home

Register where your home is: either where you live while at college in Pennsylvania (on or off campus) or your earlier Pennsylvania home if your family still lives there, as long as you have lived in that district at least 30 days before the election. You can vote only once. If you are registered at home and will be at school on Election Day, the state says to plan to apply for a mail-in or absentee ballot; you cannot vote at a polling place near campus if you are registered in another district. (official page)

At school in another state, with Pennsylvania as home

The state's pages do not speak separately to Pennsylvanians at school in another state. Its general rules: any registered voter can vote by no-excuse mail-in ballot, and the ballot must reach your county election office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. A student studying abroad who considers Pennsylvania home and plans to return counts as an overseas voter (see below). A student who moved TO Pennsylvania for college may register at the college address after living in that district at least 30 days before the election. (official page)

Military and overseas

Register and request with the federal FPCA form or Pennsylvania's forms; you can get your ballot by email. Military and overseas voters who plan to return to Pennsylvania must affirm they mailed the ballot by 11:59 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026, and the county must receive it by 5 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. A Pennsylvanian who has made a permanent home abroad (a 'federal voter') must have the ballot arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot can be used as a backup. (official page)

Pennsylvania in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Pennsylvania counts a mail ballot only if it ARRIVES by 8 p.m. on Election Day; a postmark does not help.
  • If you asked for a mail ballot but want to vote at the polls, bring the ballot and its outer envelope to be voided; otherwise you can vote only by provisional ballot. Once you have returned a mail ballot, you cannot vote at the polls.
  • The state's help line is 1-877-VOTESPA.
